quote: I'm just reaching out here about the solar form you filled out online. How are you today?
stewart_read: The intro references the form but the company identity and purpose land in a rushed, jumbled way (mistaken names 'Greg', 'Priscilla' beforehand), undermining the legitimacy-in-first-30-seconds standard.
coaching_implication: Slow the intro down and confirm identity clearly before diving into the pitch — the customer's immediate 'pertaining to what again?' shows it didn't land.

stewart_read: Customer is confused about why she's being called at all — a sign the intro did not establish legitimacy or context before the rep pushed into qualifying questions.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive failure — the rep rushed the pitch line before the intro fully registered with the customer.
coaching_implication: Pause and re-anchor legitimacy when a customer signals confusion rather than plowing ahead into the design pitch.

stewart_read: This is a spouse/family-decider-style objection variant; the rep does not probe what the grandson objected to or invert the framing, just moves to a generic reassurance.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may have judged this unrecoverable and chosen not to invest more time — but no attempt at all was made, so reactive is more supported.
coaching_implication: Ask what specifically concerned the grandson before conceding — could be cost, could be scam fear, both addressable.

stewart_read: First explicit not-interested statement; rep response is a soft reassurance about 'just building designs' rather than the schema's hello_objection small-ask or an inversion flip.
coaching_implication: Use protocols.hello_objection_not_interested phrasing — ask for 30 seconds rather than asserting no-commitment framing that doesn't address the 'why'.

quote: Okay. My husband passed away, and I can't afford it.
stewart_read: A significant vulnerability disclosure (spousal loss, affordability) is met with zero acknowledgment before the rep closes the call.
coaching_implication: Even on a call ending in disqualification, a brief 'I'm sorry to hear that' before the close is the bar — this call skipped it entirely.

stewart_read: The bill question is garbled and disconnected from any prior qualifying conversation — verify.address_homeowner, co_owner, roof, utility_company, and interest_question were all skipped per verified events, so this lands as a non-sequitur.
coaching_implication: Bill anchoring only works after rapport and context are built; jumping straight to the number with no lead-in produces confusion, not data.
